title: Hilton Jefferson: drinking buddy, Cab's punishing feature numbers
summary: Hinton asks Budd about colleagues, and Budd praises Hilton Jefferson, whom Cab would test with hard features when he was drunk.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah. I just want to ask you now, sort of wind up this whole thing, it is so beautiful about such a great life of such a tremendous musician. I'd just like to ask you a couple of things about when you came to New York there were a great deal of great musicians in New York, and just right off the top of my head, I'll call out a name, and you tell me what you thought of him, --
All right.
-- and how it was. Hilton Jefferson.
Oh, Hilton Jefferson.
Sax$phone, alto sax$phone.
He was a man that always continued to amaze me. This man -- I remember when I was with CAb --
of course, I was knowin' him before I joined Cab Calloway's band.
played Alto sax --
I had the highest respect -- and, you know, he played good clarinet too? But, you know --
And piano too, he was a piano player too.
Is that right? I never knew that about Jeff.
MR HINTON : And Coleman Hawkins. (Simultaneous remarks)
He was such a gentleman and quiet like, you would have to be with him a long time, like you did, really to know this man, I guess.
Yeah, he was one of my best friends.
He was a brilliant man too.
Right.

This guy knew all of the medical terms and everything, didn't he? But anyway, Hilton Jefferson was one of the best -- one of the finest alto saxiphone players that I know, that I ever knew, and one thing used to amaze me. Now Hilton Jefferson and myself, we were drinking buddies, as you can attest to. His favorite whiskey was Fleischmann's 90 proof, and we used to buy that Fleischmann's and drink that whiskey like Hilton like would be tore up.
Well, Cab was a friendly kind of a guy. See, Cab

would say, uh-huh, I caught him drunk. I'm going to punish him. So Cab would call like the hardest number in the book, of seven sharps, anything, and Jeff had to play a feature on that number. Hilton Jefferson would walk out on that stage and play the most beautiful solo you ever heard in your life.
Yeah, I've heard it -- agree to that
And he could never be caught off base.
(Simultaneous remarks)
-- Hilton, like I know Cab would be saying, oh, oh, I got him now. He just wanted to get him one time.
(Simultaneous remarks)

Not that he didn't love him, but he'd just say, I got to get this cat because Cab couldn't understand how can a guy be so drunk and like that and then play so doggoned beautiful, and we would play songs like Danny Boy or Willow Weep for Me and all those beautiful tunes, man, and he would just make them -- make you want to cry. When he played Danny Boy, you could see Danny Boy. We played Willow Weep for Me, I mean, you would want to cry. He was one of the greatest saxiphone players I ever heard.
